message.text:
q23.

SQL schema: `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` (the `CREATE TABLE memo` at line 33; the same table is defined per dialect in `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql` and `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql`)
Go store model: `store/memo.go` (`type Memo struct`, line 35)
API proto message: `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` (`message Memo`, line 198)
Generated frontend types: `web/src/types/proto/api/v1/memo_service_pb.ts` (`export type Memo`, line 79, with `MemoSchema` at line 204)

The SQL columns (`id`, `uid`, `creator_id`, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, `row_status`, `content`, `visibility`, `pinned`, `payload`) line up field-for-field with the Go struct, and `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` translates between the Go model and the proto message.

Two adjacent files matter if you're changing the shape. The `payload` column is not free-form JSON: its structure is defined by `MemoPayload` in `proto/store/memo.proto`, generated into Go as `storepb.MemoPayload` (the type of the struct's `Payload` field). And the Go server side of the API message is generated into `proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.go`, which is the counterpart to the frontend's `memo_service_pb.ts`.
